sections.h2: What does selling a house in Oak Lawn, Illinois involve?
sections.html:
Oak Lawn has several local steps: a village transfer stamp, a point-of-sale sewer inspection for houses, and a stamp refund program for some sellers. Each step has its own form, so starting early protects the closing date.

The village borders Chicago on the southwest side and had 58,362 residents in the 2020 census. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 56,450, a 3.2% drop from the April 2020 base. It spans about 8.6 square miles with a density near 6,800 people per square mile, which means most homes sit on compact lots.

The sections below follow the order of a typical sale: the village stamp, the sewer inspection, Cook County recording, and property tax.

The area was first called Black Oak Grove, after a road along today's 95th Street, and was settled in 1835. The Wabash Railroad brought a depot in 1880, and by 1882 the post office and station were simply Oak Lawn. The village incorporated in 1909. Growth jumped after World War II, and by 1960 nearly 20,000 people lived here.

On April 21, 1967, a tornado cut through the village, damaging or destroying roughly 900 buildings and killing more than 30 people. Rebuilding drove another round of growth, and the population peaked at about 63,500 in the mid-1970s. Since 2002 the downtown stretch of 95th Street has been redeveloped with condominium buildings, shops, a Metra station expansion and a parking garage.

  • Advocate Christ Medical Center is one of the largest hospitals and Level I trauma centers in the state.
  • Metra's SouthWest Service runs from the Oak Lawn station toward downtown Chicago.
  • Elementary schools include Kolb, Lieb, Harnew, Columbus Manor, Covington, Hannum, Hometown, Kolmar and Sward, with Simmons and Oak Lawn-Hometown as middle schools.
  • Oak Lawn Community High School and Harold L. Richards High School are the two public high schools.

sections.h2: How does the Oak Lawn transfer stamp work?
sections.html:
The Cook County Clerk's October 2025 list shows an Oak Lawn tax of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, enacted January 1, 1982, with the seller liable and an exemption letter attached to the recording as proof. Exempt transfers pay no fee. The village adds that senior sellers of a primary residence are now exempt, with the rules in section 3 of its exemption list.

  • Request stamps or an exemption letter from the Finance Department. The village accepts only electronic fillable forms, and handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Questions go to 708-499-7775 or transferstamps@oaklawn-il.gov.
  • A Utility Billing Account Change form handles the water account.
  • The village's own address on the Clerk's list is 9446 S. Raymond St., phone 708.636.4400.

State and county taxes sit on top: 50 cents per $500 for the state under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and 25 cents per $500 for Cook County.

sections.h2: What is the sewer inspection and how do I schedule it?
sections.html:
Oak Lawn requires a sewer inspection, called I&I, for single-family homes and qualifying townhomes before the transfer stamp. The village recommends scheduling well ahead of closing.

  1. Use the village's online permit portal, search the property address, choose Residential and the Transfer Stamp Sewer Inspection (I&I) permit type, and enter N/A for work details.
  2. The village reviews the request and emails either a record number with a scheduling link or a note that no inspection is needed.
  3. Pick a date for the I&I Sewer inspection. It happens between 10am and 2pm, and someone over 18 must be present with access to the interior.
  4. After the inspection, a payment link arrives by email for $100, and the results follow once payment is made.

Ask the village's Finance Department at 708-499-7775 whether your address needs the inspection, since the village screens each request first.

sections.h2: Can I get some transfer stamp money back?
sections.html:
Yes, in three cases under village ordinance 3-2-7, each requiring the seller to have owned and lived in the house as a principal residence without renting any part of it.

  • Reinvestment: buy or build a single-family home or condominium inside the village within one year of paying the tax, and live there.
  • Senior citizens: a one-time refund for a seller age 65 or older who owned and occupied the home for more than one year, with a rule for co-owners under 60.
  • Family sale: sell to a child, parent, grandparent, brother, sister or grandchild, step relatives included.

Refund requests are due within one year of the sale. Packets for each case are linked from the village's refund page, and the Finance Department's refund line is 708-499-7777.

sections.h2: How does Cook County assessment and recording apply?
sections.html:
Oak Lawn deeds are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St. The Clerk lists the seller as liable for both the state and county stamps. A PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

For assessments, look up your 14-digit PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to see your township. The south and west suburban townships follow a triennial cycle with reassessments in 2023 and 2026. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for installment status on the parcel, and expect the title company to prorate the year's bill at closing.

sections.h2: What do buyers see in Oak Lawn parks and daily life?
sections.html:
The village maintains 22 parks on more than 300 acres. Centennial Park alone covers 38 acres, and the park system includes outdoor pools, an indoor ice arena, two fitness centers, an indoor racquet center and an 18-hole golf course. Oak Lawn's public library began in 1934 with a collection of one hundred books.

Broadband subscriptions reach 91.3% of households in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, and the median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,000 a month. Those are useful points when a buyer weighs a house here against a rental.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits an Oak Lawn house?
sections.html: An updated house near 95th Street or the Metra station usually does well in a listing. A house with sewer problems, an old rental history or an estate behind it often fits a direct as-is sale better, since the inspection and stamp steps still apply either way.

faqs.q: Does Oak Lawn charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Cook County Clerk's list shows a village rate of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, paid by the seller, with exempt transfers needing an exemption letter. Contact the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 for the stamp.

faqs.q: What does the Oak Lawn sewer inspection cost?
faqs.a: The village charges $100, paid by a link emailed after the inspection. It applies to single-family homes and qualifying townhomes and runs between 10am and 2pm.

faqs.q: Are seniors exempt from the transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The village states that seniors selling a primary residence are now exempt, with details in section 3 of its exemption list. A separate refund route exists for sellers 65 or older under ordinance 3-2-7.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ask for a stamp refund?
faqs.a: Refunds must be requested within one year of the date of sale. The village lists reinvestment, senior and immediate family cases, each with its own packet.

faqs.q: Where is an Oak Lawn deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The sale also needs the PTAX-203 declaration and stamped deed.
